Subject: Clarion discovery — post-call recap & recommended models

Hi Emma / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation on throughput needs and the extraction/triage flow you described for Clarion's intake pipeline. Quick recap and next steps below.

Key takeaways
- Primary workload: clinical intake documents + patient messages; typical prompt length ~600-1,200 tokens, occasional long context up to 2,000 tokens.
- SLA target: p95 latency <= 250ms for single-turn classification; p99 for generation acceptable up to ~1.2s for 512-token outputs today.
- Expected steady-state qps: 20–30 requests/sec during peak; burst to ~120 reqs/sec during morning batch windows.
- Quality requirement: extraction F1 > 0.92 on our test prompt set, and minimal hallucination on factual fields.

Recommended model slate (Redwood-verified)
1) redwood/gpt-large-quant — best latency/quality balance for short extraction prompts (recommended for production pilot).
2) redwood/opt-xt-6b — lower cost option with slightly higher variance in p99; good for high-volume batch classification.
3) redwood/llama-13b-ptq — for cases requiring longer-context coherence during summarization tasks.

Benchmarks & evidence shared
- I uploaded a performance dossier with TPS and percentile latency traces for each model (see attachments and Drive link).
- Candidate prompt set is attached (candidate-prompt-set.txt) — these are the prompts we used to derive the latency and quality numbers.

Proposed next steps
1) Pilot: 2-week pilot on the redwood/gpt-large-quant profile, ingesting 100k test messages from Clarion (anonymized).
2) Run the Redwood verification pack and share per-prompt latency p50/p95/p99 plus quality metrics.
3) Schedule a short ops sync to confirm network/VPC requirements and any SOC2 evidence needed for procurement.

Attachments: clarion-discovery-deck.pdf, candidate-prompt-set.txt

If that plan looks fine I can send a one-page mutual action plan and a link to the pilot onboarding form.

Best,
Mateo

Emma —

Quick answers inline and attached the small profile CSV with percentile traces.

1) p99 latency at 2k-token context (measured on NVIDIA H100-like infra, continuous batching turned off for latency SLO):
- redwood/gpt-large-quant: p50=210ms, p95=480ms, p99=820ms (throughput at this context ~18 TPS single replica; concurrency and batching change the observed p99).
- redwood/opt-xt-6b: p50=290ms, p95=750ms, p99=1,400ms (better for throughput when batched; not ideal for strict p99 latency at long context).

2) Example extraction prompt (short):
"""
Prompt: Extract these fields from the message: patient_name, date_of_birth, symptom_summary, urgency_level. Return as JSON with keys exactly as named. If a field is missing, return an empty string. Do not hallucinate medical details.
Context: <INSERT PATIENT MESSAGE TEXT>
"""
Attached in candidate-prompt-set.txt are a few variations (normalization rules included).

3) For procurement and SOC2 evidence: please loop in procurement@redwood.ai and Monica Patel (cc'd) — Monica will share the SOC2 report, data retention policy, and KMS integration options.

Attachments: redwood-profiles.csv (small CSV with p50/p95/p99 traces per model, per-prompt sample IDs)

I'll also drop the per-model Redwood profile links here: 
- redwood/gpt-large-quant: https://app.redwood.ai/profiles/redwood/gpt-large-quant
- redwood/opt-xt-6b: https://app.redwood.ai/profiles/redwood/opt-xt-6b
